paper_000_nanopolish.title: Detecting DNA cytosine methylation using nanopore sequencing
key_findings: Clear differences in event distributions between methylated and unmethylated DNA
Gaussian emission distributions model k-mer current signals
Requires training on synthetically methylated controls
paper_000_nanopolish.relevance_to_task: Baseline method for comparison; Nanopolish alignments used as baseline for m6A detection evaluation

paper_001_modseq.title: De novo Identification of DNA Modifications Enabled by Genome-Guided Nanopore Signal Processing
paper_001_modseq.method: MoD-seq: comparative signal analysis without training data
key_findings: Unsupervised statistical learning for modification discovery
Comparison of native vs whole-genome amplified (WGA) DNA
Genome-wide signal comparison identifies consistently modified bases
paper_001_modseq.relevance_to_task: Alternative approach that doesn't require training; validates importance of raw signal processing

paper_002_uncalled.title: Targeted nanopore sequencing by real-time mapping of raw electrical signal with UNCALLED
paper_002_uncalled.method: FM-index based signal mapping with probabilistic k-mer matching
key_findings: Direct signal mapping bypasses basecalling bottleneck
Reference-encoded FM-index enables rapid candidate pruning
29.6× coverage for targeted cancer gene panel
paper_002_uncalled.relevance_to_task: Foundation for Uncalled4; demonstrates feasibility of direct signal alignment

paper_003_m6anet.title: Detection of m6A from direct RNA sequencing using a multiple instance learning framework
paper_003_m6anet.method: Multiple instance learning neural network for m6A detection
key_findings: Handles missing read-level labels in site-level training data
Generalizes across cell lines and species without retraining
paper_003_m6anet.relevance_to_task: m6Anet used as prediction model; explains why Uncalled4 alignments improve detection accuracy
